intro:
Use it to show who someone is: the author of a comment, the people on a team, who has read a document. It shows `src` once the picture has loaded, and until then, or if it never loads, the initials of `name`.

The initials sit on a tint of one of the theme's chart colours, picked from the name. The same person gets the same colour everywhere, so a list of people without pictures can still be told apart.

A badge and an overlapping avatar are cut out of the avatar beneath them, not drawn with a ring. The gap shows whatever the avatar sits on, so it works on a card, a tinted row or a photograph without a colour to match.

`name` is also what a screen reader says, with the badge's status after it. Pass `alt` when something else should be said.
usage:
<Avatar src="/photos/khalid.jpg" name="Khalid Abdi" />

<Avatar name="Kofi Mensah" size="lg">
  <Avatar.Badge status="online" />
</Avatar>

<Avatar.Group max={4} label="Read by">
  {people.map((person) => (
    <Avatar key={person.id} src={person.photo} name={person.name} />
  ))}
</Avatar.Group>

parts.Badge: A dot or a small icon on the avatar's lower trailing edge. `status` draws a presence dot: `online`, `away`, `busy`, or a hollow `offline`. For an icon, such as a check on a verified account, pass the icon as children and a `color`. `label` is what a screen reader says after the name.
parts.Group: A row of avatars overlapping one another. It sets the `size` and `shape` of every avatar in it. Hovered or focused, it opens up so each face can be seen whole. Past `max`, the rest are counted in a last circle that opens a list of their names.

examples.title: Sizes and shapes
examples.description: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl`. `circle` is for people. `square` is for teams, projects and things, with corners that grow with the size.

examples.title: Without a picture
examples.description: Each name lands on a colour of its own. A picture that fails to load falls back to the initials. `fallback` replaces the initials with something else, such as an icon for a bot, and with no name at all the avatar shows a person's outline.

examples.title: Badges
examples.description: `status` draws a presence dot, and `offline` is hollow. A badge can hold an icon instead, such as a check on a verified account. The gap round a badge is cut through the avatar, not painted, so it shows whatever the avatar sits on.

examples.title: Groups
examples.description: Hover over a group, or move focus into it, and it opens up. Press the count to see who it stands for. In a group of `square` avatars, each is cut round the shape of the one over it.

notes:
### Loading

The initials show from the start and the picture replaces them once it has loaded, so nothing flickers between an empty circle and a face.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion turned on, a group does not open up when hovered.

### In a group

A group is a `role="group"`. Give it a `label` that says who the people are, such as "Members" or "Read by".
